key_insight: Without a shared quantum reference frame, a learner cannot assign distinct labels to unseen quantum directions, so states outside the training span collapse to the same prediction.
engineering_relevance: Quantum ML systems need explicit physical structure—such as measurement bases, feature maps, symmetry priors, or diverse training states—to generalize beyond the training data.
method: Formulate supervised learning without an external quantum reference frame.
Prove symmetry constraints force identical predictions for all pure states orthogonal to the training span.
Derive a robust extension showing weak symmetry breaking only partially relaxes the collapse, with multiqubit generic concepts needing exponentially many oriented training directions.
evidence_signal: The paper combines theoretical proofs with numerical illustrations that visualize prediction collapse and its controlled relaxation.
watch_item: Performance can appear misleadingly strong on known subspaces, but generalization fails if the training set does not provide enough orientation or span the relevant Hilbert space.
paper_title: No Reference-Free Generalization in Quantum Machine Learning
